text: Skip to Content POETRY FICTION ESSAY TRANSLATION BOOKMOOD ABOUT SUBMIT/FAQ EBROHIMIE ROAD is now Available to Watch Online This July [WATCH HERE] Olongo Press July 6, 2026 Download as PDF This July, Nobel Laureate Wole Soyinka turns 92. In his honour, Olongo Africa is making Ebrohimie Road: a Museum of Memory available to watch online for free for seven days. The documentary film, produced by OlongoAfrica, directed by Kọ́lá Túbọ̀sún and shot by veteran filmmaker Tunde Kelani examines how the personal story of one man and one family became the story of the whole nation at a crucial time. In Ebrohimie Road, which doubles as an exploration of history and an exhumation of what is lost, Túbọ̀sún discovers not just a hidden part of Nigerian literary, cultural, and political history, but also how ecological changes contribute to the erosion of memory. From July 7 to July 13, Ebrohimie Road: a Museum of Memory will be available to watch online, at OlongoAfrica, for free. For those who haven’t seen this award-winning film, this is your chance to share in its journey. For those who have seen it before, this is your chance to see it again. The free screening is over! Thank you for watching. You can still continue to see the film here on Vimeo. <p class="wp-block-paragraph">This July, Nobel Laureate Wole Soyinka turns 92. In his honour, Olongo Africa is making <em>Ebrohimie Road: a Museum of Memory</em> available to watch online for free for seven days.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">The documentary film, produced by OlongoAfrica, directed by Kọ́lá Túbọ̀sún and shot by veteran filmmaker Tunde Kelani examines how the personal story of one man and one family became the story of the whole nation at a crucial time. In <em>Ebrohimie Road</em>, which doubles as an exploration of history and an exhumation of what is lost, Túbọ̀sún discovers not just a hidden part of Nigerian literary, cultural, and political history, but also how ecological changes contribute to the erosion of memory.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">From July 7 to July 13, <em>Ebrohimie Road: a Museum of Memory</em> will be available to watch online, at OlongoAfrica, for free. For those who haven’t seen this award-winning film, this is your chance to share in its journey. For those who have seen it before, this is your chance to see it again.</p>



<p class="alignfull wp-block-paragraph"><em><strong>The free screening is over</strong></em>! Thank you for watching. You can still continue to see the film <a href="https://vimeo.com/ondemand/ebrohimieroad">here on Vimeo</a>.</p>
